title: Consequences of Idolatry
english: The axe lies at the root of the trees; every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
Since Israel has become hardened and recently devoted to idolatrous worship, God, through the prophet, foretells the future capture of Jerusalem.

He says, 'What has happened to you now, that you have all gone up to empty houses? The city is filled with wailing; your wounded are not wounded by the sword, nor are your dead from war' (Isaiah 22:2).

It seems that this refers to the devastation in the time of Jehoniah, as they blame those from Israel as if they did not even know evil, and thus they are overcome by extremely difficult troubles, knowing what is to come.
For they should have been mourning and lamenting, going up to the house of God, promising repentance, asking for remembrance of their sins, and seeking help from Him alone.

And he himself taught this, saying through one of the holy prophets: 'Gird yourselves and lament, you priests; wail, you ministers of the altar; enter, sleep in sackcloth, you ministers of God, for the grain offering and the drink offering have ceased from your house; sanctify a fast, proclaim a healing, gather all the elders living in the land to the house of your God, and cry out to the Lord intensely, Alas, alas, for the day' (Joel 1:14).
These are indeed the things they should have been doing to appease the one who is able to save, being provoked.
However, they did not even consider doing what was necessary, but rather they went up to their useless houses, where there were lamentations and wailing of children, perhaps due to hunger and thirst.
This is what inevitably happens to cities under siege.

He says: 'What has happened to you now, that you have all gone up to empty houses?' For why, he asks, in such inescapable terrors, and because of the words concerning your end, and the whole struggle, have you not cried out to God, but have instead fled to empty houses, even though it benefits you nothing?
For this reason, he says they are empty houses.
And why was the city filled with wailing? Not that they cried out to God, but rather they wailed in vain, and they were only being harmed by the evils occurring within the gates.
The lamentation should have been for repentance, and the tears should have been shed before God.
Behold, he says, before the battle began, before the sword was drawn, before the resistance was planned, the city was already full of dead bodies.

title: Tyre's Defense and Destruction
english: They were fortifying themselves, keeping themselves outside of all access, and declaring themselves better than the Babylonians.

In another way, the Jewish nation was also being destroyed, having been worn down and plundered, and the remaining ones were being taken; and they were setting up sacred vessels to false gods, and sending away those who had been under the yoke of their slavery.

God spoke through one of the holy prophets, saying, 'What have you to do with me, Tyre and Sidon, and all Galilee of the foreigners? Do you repay me? Do you take vengeance on me? I will quickly repay you, and I will take back my silver and gold, and my chosen and beautiful things, which you took and brought into your temples, and you sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Israel to the sons of the Greeks, so that you might drive them out of their borders' (Isaiah 23:18).
Tyre was an island, with a narrow strait in the middle, and not far from the mainland.
When the Babylonian came, seeking to take it along with the other cities, he ordered his armies to fill in the sea between, to join it to the mainland, and not to leave it an island.

As the Babylonians were about to capture Tyre, the majority of its inhabitants, who were engaged in commerce and accustomed to sailing, took their families and departed from the island to other cities and villages.
Most of the people, including the most prominent ones, escaped with their ships, and the Babylonians were not moderately grieved to learn that they had done so.
The Babylonians then entered the city, killing those who remained, taking many captive, and doing what was customary for victors.

The prophet Ezekiel had foretold this event, and God had spoken to him about the fate of Tyre, saying that Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, had subjected his power to great servitude against the city, but had not received any reward for his labor, and instead, God gave him the land of Egypt (Ezekiel 29:18).
After the capture of Tyre, the Babylonian turned his war against the Egyptian nation.
The prophet Isaiah now recalls this history and commands the ships of Carthage to wail because Tyre was lost and no longer receives visitors from the land of the Kittim.

title: Consequences of Disobedience
english: Because they have transgressed the law and changed the commandments, thus violating the eternal covenant, a curse will devour the earth, since those who dwell on it have sinned.

The earth will mourn because its inhabitants have transgressed the law and loosened the eternal covenant, and the prophet declares that the earth will be deserted, for those who dwell on it have sinned.

It seems that the prophet, having punished other cities and the land of the Jews, now brings the faults of those under the law to the forefront, as they have transgressed the law, considering it as nothing, and have turned to human commandments.
In doing so, they have trampled the natural law engraved on them by God, which teaches them to know good and evil, for God, the creator of all, has made man from the beginning.

This natural law guides us towards knowledge of good and evil, and it is what is said through the voice of John about the only-begotten Son of God, that He is the true light, which enlightens every man coming into the world (John 1:9).

We believe that this will happen in the last times, according to the words of the visitation, and as it is written, 'in those days, the Lord says, giving my laws into their mind and writing them upon their hearts' (Jeremiah 31:33).
However, those on earth have transgressed this innate law and changed the commandments, for being esteemed for good works, they turned towards love of flesh and earthly wisdom.
As a result, the earth became cursed, and its inhabitants provoked the Creator through numerous transgressions, which is why the people of the earth will be impoverished, and only a few will remain.

This is because the earth has become cursed due to the abundance of lawlessness within it, and its inhabitants will be burdened with unexpected poverty, barely surviving; only a few countable people will be left.
Ultimately, those who will be condemned for their many transgressions on the divine throne will certainly be impoverished and in need.
